circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi spans 5. 281 kilometers and was designed by Hermann Tilke. Since 2009, it has served as the venue for the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, which concludes the Formula One season, making it the second Middle Eastern track after Bahrain, followed later by circuits in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street-based motorsport venue located around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb and holds an FIA Grade 1 licence. It hosts the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year, along with the Supercars Championship event and various supporting racing categories.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: The Red Bull Ring is a 4. 326 km Austrian motorsport facility located in Spielberg, Styria, which previously operated as the Österreichring and hosted the nation's Grand Prix annually from 1970 to 1987. Following a significant reconfiguration and rebranding as the A1-Ring, the venue returned to the Grand Prix calendar from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital, stretching 6. 003 km to rank as the fourth-longest venue on the F1 calendar. After hosting the 2016 European Grand Prix as its inaugural F1 event, the circuit established its own Azerbaijan Grand Prix the following year.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix that same year. The venue, which holds an FIA Grade 1 license and features multiple track configurations, accommodates various motorsport categories including GP2 racing, endurance competitions, and drag racing events.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, is a 4. 657 km track featuring a balanced mix of lengthy straights and diverse corner types that make it a versatile test for racing machinery. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Spa is a 7. 004 km Belgian circuit situated near the town of Spa in Wallonia that has served as the home of the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix since 1950, when it featured in the inaugural F1 season. The venue has maintained continuous Grand Prix status from 1985 onward, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006, establishing itself as one of motorsport's historic and enduring racing destinations.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Montreal's Notre Dame Island, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km track that serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue has accommodated various other major motorsport series including sports car racing championships and North American racing competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport facility is primarily recognized as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix, which took place annually from 2004 until 2019 before returning in 2024. The track has expanded its racing calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix series beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone, located in Northamptonshire, England, has been the primary venue for the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After sharing the prestigious event with Aintree and Brands Hatch between 1955 and 1986, the circuit became the permanent home of the British Grand Prix from 1987 onwards, while also hosting the MotoGP British round.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted Formula One's inaugural grand prix in the Eastern Bloc when it opened in 1986. Built in just eight months, the track was constructed outside the city near a highway after government authorities rejected plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit built in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. The track has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, earning its nickname "the Temple of Speed" from its characteristic long straights and fast-corner design.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, Japan, spans 5. 807 kilometers and accommodates up to 155,000 spectators. The track is renowned for hosting prestigious Formula One and Super Formula races, making it one of motorsport's most significant venues.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, following the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding urban landscape. The track weaves past iconic destinations including major hotel and casino properties, as well as distinctive landmarks like MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km track in Mexico City, named after brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez who both died in racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix during multiple eras, resuming as a regular calendar fixture in 2015 on its current configuration after a 23-year absence.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida, spanning 3. 363 miles with 19 turns and an average qualifying speed of approximately 139 mph. Created by renowned track designers Apex Circuit Design, the venue hosts the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar beginning in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Monaco Grand Prix circuit winds through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine in the principality, spanning 3. 337 kilometers around the harbor. Though officially known as the Circuit de Monaco, it is widely called "Monte Carlo" since most of the track runs through that specific district.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, this 4. 259 km circuit hosted motorsport racing for decades before rejoining the Formula One calendar in 2021 with the reinstatement of the Dutch Grand Prix. The partnership between the track and Formula One will conclude following the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Qatari racing facility situated near Lusail, just north of Doha, spanning 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise circuit in São Paulo, Brazil, originally opened in 1940 and renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal plane crash eight years earlier. The venue has hosted numerous Grand Prix races and features additional karting facilities dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: A street circuit situated along Jeddah's waterfront promenade beside the Red Sea, this venue has served as the home of Saudi Arabia's Formula One Grand Prix since its inaugural running in 2021. The track also began hosting a Formula E race starting in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a temporary road course that winds through Singapore's Marina Bay area, incorporating portions of the Downtown Core and Kallang districts.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner types, making it suitable for testing multiple racing disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located near Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. The track has hosted numerous racing series beyond F1, including NASCAR, MotoGP, and endurance racing competitions like the FIA World Endurance Championship's Lone Star Le Mans event.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver who represents Thailand on the Formula One grid, currently competing for the Williams team.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championships during his tenure with Renault in 2005 and 2006 while accumulating 32 race victories across his 23-season career. Beyond Formula One, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, winning the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship and claiming multiple victories at prestigious events including the 24 Hours of Le Mans twice and the 24 Hours of Daytona, making him the sole driver to have won both a Formula One championship and the world endurance drivers' title.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured six Grand Prix victories since joining the grid in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British driver currently racing in Formula One for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabi Bortoleto, a Brazilian racing driver, currently competes in Formula One as a member of the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas, a Finnish driver, currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after a lengthy career spanning 13 seasons and featuring ten race victories. He achieved runner-up finishes in the championship standings in both 2019 and 2020 while driving for Mercedes.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently competing in Formula One with Alpine, bringing South American representation to the sport's top racing series.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian motorsport competitor, holds a reserve driver position with Haas in Formula One while actively racing in European endurance competition. He has participated in seven Formula One races across the 2024 and 2025 seasons.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri remains a career highlight for the driver.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Hadjar is a French-Algerian motorsport competitor who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, representing France internationally.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding an unprecedented seven world championship titles that he shares with Michael Schumacher. His extensive record collection includes the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved significant success in endurance motorsport, securing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand racing driver, currently competes in Formula One as a member of the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver currently races for Ferrari in Formula One, having accumulated nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine-season career. Leclerc finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while competing for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver who returned to Formula One from 2022 to 2024 after an earlier stint in the sport from 2014 to 2020. Currently, he competes in the World Endurance Championship as a factory BMW driver for WRT, while also participating part-time in NASCAR's top series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris represents Great Britain in Formula One competition for McLaren, where he claimed the 2025 drivers' championship. The British driver has accumulated 12 Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season tenure in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French racing driver currently competing in Formula One for Haas. The accomplished driver previously secured a victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing experience from 15 seasons and six Grand Prix victories. He achieved his career-best result in 2023 when he finished second in the drivers' championship while competing for Red Bull.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having claimed nine Grand Prix victories since joining the grid.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career before retiring from the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured seven Grand Prix victories during his eight-season tenure in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, having accumulated four Grand Prix victories during his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, having previously driven in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently competing for Aston Martin in the sport's top racing series.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver currently functioning as a reserve for both Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls. He participated in Formula One competition across a five-year span from 2021 through 2025.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: A Dutch and Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing under the Dutch flag, Verstappen has secured four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024, alongside 71 Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver currently serving as a reserve driver for Cadillac in Formula One. He competed in the championship from 2022 to 2024 and holds the distinction of being the sole Chinese driver to have raced in the sport.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has raced as Alpine since 2021, continuing Renault's factory Formula One programme following a rebranding to highlight the sports car marque. Operating with a Mercedes power unit, the squad achieved its sole Alpine-era victory through Esteban Ocon in Hungary 2021, before Renault's departure from the sport concluded their long-term involvement at the end of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automobile manufacturer, has competed in Formula One through different organizational structures, with the present iteration operating under AMR GP Limited as Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, participating continuously in the World Championship since its inception in 1950. The squad, colloquially referred to by their emblem's imagery, has established itself as the sport's most dominant force throughout its seven-decade history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One team founded by NASCAR owner Gene Haas in 2014, TGR Haas F1 Team entered the sport in 2016. Currently led by principal Ayao Komatsu following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, the team has operated since its inception with a focus on competitive single-seater racing.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, this Swiss engineering firm initially excelled in endurance racing, winning the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours and two world championships before transitioning to Formula One in 1993. Over three decades as an independent constructor, the team competed in the sport until 2025, ranking as the fourth-longest-running constructor by race entries, before being acquired by Audi AG in 2024 to serve as the foundation for the manufacturer's F1 programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that operates as a subsidiary within the larger McLaren Group. The team currently competes under sponsorship naming rights in the sport's premier championship.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with its current team based in Brackley and operating under a German licence. The squad, known colloquially as the Silver Arrows, became jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and Toto Wolff from January 2022. The team competes as Mercedes-AMG Petronas in the championship.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor based in Faenza that entered the sport in 2024 as one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned outfits, alongside the primary Red Bull Racing operation. The squad maintains a secondary facility in Milton Keynes in proximity to its sister team, establishing itself as part of the Austrian conglomerate's two-team Formula One strategy.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor established in 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull-owned squads in the sport. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the team functions as a sister operation alongside Red Bull Racing within the Austrian conglomerate's motorsport portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, based in England but licensed under Austria, represents one of two Formula One operations controlled by Red Bull GmbH. Since its establishment in 2005, the team operated under Christian Horner's leadership until his 2025 departure, when Laurent Mekies assumed the managerial role.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, evolved from Williams's previous failed racing venture and remains headquartered at its Grove, Oxfordshire facility. Competing as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in 2026, the organization operates from a substantial 60-acre estate and continues as both team and constructor in the championship.
